stories.title: Genting Lands $500M to Refi Mixed-Use Omni Center in Miami
stories.excerpt: Genting Americas scored a $500 million loan to refinance the mixed-use Omni Center near Downtown Miami, three years after failing to sell the 15-acre site next door for $1.2 billion. The 1.5 million-square-foot Omni Center is between 1501 and 1645 Biscayne Boulevard, just north of the entrance to the MacArthur and Venetian causeways, near the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts. Wells Fargo is serving as an administrative agent on behalf of a group of lenders, according to public mortgage documents. The property, which was built in the 1970s, features 435,000 square feet of office space, a 527-room Hilton hotel and a 2,500-spot parking garage. Omni International Mall, located inside the building, closed in 2000. Over the past year, Planet Fitness signed a 26,000-square-foot office lease and consulting firm Skyline Financial took 25,420 square feet. Other tenants include the U.S. State Department, which operates a passport office, and Keypoint Academy, which operates a private grade school. Genting Americas, a division of Malaysian casino operator Genting Group, purchased the asset for $180 million in 2011 through foreclosure. That same year, it also bought the neighboring 15-acre site for $236 million, creating one of the biggest assemblages in Miami. The firm demolished the office building on that neighboring site, home to the Miami Herald headquarters, with plans to develop a casino, which never materialized after it failed to gain a gambling license. In 2023, a joint venture, led by David Martin’s Terra, went under contract to buy the waterfront assemblage, not including the Omni Center, for $1.2 billion in what would have been one of the country’s priciest land acquisitions. But the transaction fell apart as the developer struggled to secure financing, and the land remains mostly vacant today. A representative for Genting Americas did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Genting refinances $500M on 1.5M SF Omni Center Miami; Wells Fargo syndication.
Mixed-use asset (office, hotel, retail, parking) attracting new tenants despite 1970s vintage.
Recent leases: Planet Fitness 26K SF, Skyline Financial 25.4K SF office space.
stories.summary: Genting Americas closed a $500 million refinance on the Omni Center (1.5M SF) near downtown Miami via Wells Fargo syndication. The 1970s-era mixed-use property contains 435K SF office, 527-room Hilton, 2,500-space garage, and ground-floor retail. Recent tenant wins include Planet Fitness (26K SF) and Skyline Financial (25.4K SF), alongside government and education tenants.
stories.impact: Refinance success signals lender confidence in Miami's downtown office-to-mixed-use conversion pipeline and sustained demand for urban mixed-use anchoring. Biscayne Blvd's tenant activity (Planet Fitness, Skyline Financial) and proximity to cultural/government draws (Arsht Center, State Dept) validate adaptive reuse thesis—relevant for Trammell Crow's multifamily + mixed-use development strategies in South Florida urban cores.

stories.title: AT&T Signs Five-Year Extension on Retail Space at 3 Times Square
stories.excerpt: Rudin said Wednesday that AT&T has signed a five-year extension of its retail lease at 3 Times Square. The telecom giant occupies a 6,623-square-foot Times Square location that includes a ground-floor storefront on Seventh Avenue between 42nd and 43rd Streets and lower-level space. The renewal follows Rudin’s lease with global jewelry brand Pandora, which will open at street level later this year. “Times Square remains one of the world’s most dynamic and heavily trafficked retail corridors in the world, and AT&T’s renewed commitment at 3 Times Square reinforces its spot at the center of it all,” said Kevin Daly, VP of commercial leasing at Rudin. Rudin was represented in-house by Daly and Craig Panzirer, SVP, head of office leasing. AT&T was represented by Loren Baron of CBRE. Rudin and joint venture partner Thomson Reuters recently completed an extensive capital improvement program at 3 Times Square, which originally opened in 2001. The post AT&T Signs Five-Year Extension on Retail Space at 3 Times Square appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AT&T extends 5-year retail lease at 3 Times Square; 6,623 SF on Seventh Ave.
Rudin/Thomson Reuters completed major capital improvements; Pandora opening at street level.
Times Square retail remains anchored by major corporate tenants despite office weakness.
stories.summary: AT&T renewed a five-year retail lease at 3 Times Square in Midtown Manhattan for 6,623 SF spanning ground floor and lower level on Seventh Avenue. The renewal follows Rudin and Thomson Reuters completing a capital improvement program and signals continued retail stabilization as Pandora prepares to open at street level.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily; office/retail story. However, Times Square's ability to retain major corporate retail tenants (AT&T) and attract luxury brands (Pandora) suggests midtown foot traffic and mixed-use activation remain robust, supporting ground-floor retail economics for multifamily+retail developments in Manhattan's high-barrier markets.

stories.title: Barings Provides $139M Refi on Hillwood Industrial Campus
stories.excerpt: Barings has provided $138.6 million in first mortgage financing to refinance the first phase of Speedway Commerce Center, consisting of two Class A industrial buildings totaling approximately 656,000 square feet in Rancho Cucamonga. The financing was provided to Hillwood. “We are pleased to provide this financing to Hillwood, a best-in-class industrial developer with a long track record of delivering high-quality logistics assets in key distribution markets,” said Tom Cross, managing director at Barings. “Speedway Commerce Center is a modern, strategically located industrial asset in one of the country’s most sought-after logistics markets, with excellent transportation connectivity and strong long-term demand drivers.” Fully leased, Speedway Commerce Center offers high clear heights, ample trailer and automobile parking, and extensive loading capabilities. It is located with immediate access to Interstate 10 and Interstate 15, providing connectivity throughout Southern California and access to the Ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach. The post Barings Provides $139M Refi on Hillwood Industrial Campus appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Barings finances $138.6M refi on Speedway Commerce Center, Rancho Cucamonga; fully leased.
Two Class A industrial buildings, 656K SF, with Interstate 10/15 access to LA/Long Beach ports.
Hillwood developer; strong logistics fundamentals cited as underwriting driver.
stories.summary: Barings provided $138.6 million in first mortgage financing to Hillwood for the refinance of Phase 1 of Speedway Commerce Center in Rancho Cucamonga, comprising two Class A industrial buildings totaling 656K SF. The fully leased asset offers strategic highway connectivity and proximity to major California ports.
stories.impact: Industrial logistics strength and lender appetite do not directly affect multifamily; however, robust Inland Empire industrial demand (Rancho Cucamonga) implies sustained employment and population retention in the region, supporting long-term multifamily demand drivers and rent resilience in the broader LA/IE market.

stories.title: Gilbane Development Acquires Sheepshead Bay Site Suited to Large-Scale Affordable Housing
stories.excerpt: Ariel Property Advisors has arranged the $37-million sale of 2185 Coyle St., a mixed-use development site offering 408,400 buildable square feet on a 96,000-square-foot lot in the Sheepshead Bay neighborhood of Brooklyn. The recently rezoned property is ideally suited for a large-scale affordable housing development. An Ariel team comprised of founding partners Victor Sozio and Michael A. Tortorici; partner Sean R. Kelly, president and founder Shimon Shkury and director Remi Mandell arranged the transaction on behalf of the seller, a joint venture between AAG Management and ABS Partners. Gilbane Development acquired the property. “The recent rezoning created a significant opportunity to bring new affordable housing development to the Sheepshead Bay neighborhood,” said Sozio. “The site’s scale and development potential made it an attractive opportunity for the buyer and we were pleased to work with all parties to facilitate this transaction.” The post Gilbane Development Acquires Sheepshead Bay Site Suited to Large-Scale Affordable Housing appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Gilbane Development acquires Sheepshead Bay site; $37M for 96K SF lot, 408.4K buildable SF.
Recent rezoning enables large-scale affordable housing; 4.25 FAR potential on mixed-use.
Brooklyn affordable housing pipeline accelerating post-rezoning entitlement.
stories.summary: Ariel Property Advisors arranged the $37 million sale of 2185 Coyle Street in Brooklyn's Sheepshead Bay neighborhood to Gilbane Development. The 96K SF lot offers 408.4K buildable SF and was recently rezoned to enable large-scale affordable housing development on a strategically underutilized waterfront-adjacent site.
stories.impact: Direct signal of Brooklyn affordable housing demand and entitlement momentum post-rezoning. Recent zoning changes lowering barriers to density suggest regulatory tailwinds for multifamily development in outer-borough transit-adjacent sites; Sheepshead Bay represents emerging value-creation window for affordable/workforce housing—key for Trammell Crow's mission-driven development in NYC.

stories.title: JV Acquires Seniors Facility in San Diego’s Clairemont Neighborhood
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap arranged the sale of Canyon Villas, a 122-unit, 122-operating bed, independent living, assisted living and memory care facility with 133 licensed beds in the Clairemont neighborhood of San Diego. Pricing was not disclosed. “Our marketing process on Canyon Villas generated multiple high-quality offers and provided the buyer with a compelling value-add opportunity in a highly sought after San Diego submarket,” said Hap Knowles, director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s Orange County office. “With improving operational efficiencies and meaningful rent growth potential, the community is well-positioned to deliver steady, long-term cash flow and a strong foundation for future value creation.” Knowles, Nick Stahler, and Michael Mooney of Marcus & Millichap, in association with Tony Solomon, Marcus & Millichap’s California broker of record, represented the seller, San Diego Christian Foundation, and procured the buyer, a regional private equity group in a joint venture with a local operator. The post JV Acquires Seniors Facility in San Diego’s Clairemont Neighborhood appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Regional PE JV acquires Canyon Villas, San Diego seniors facility; 122 units, 122 beds.
Independent/assisted living + memory care in Clairemont (high-demand submarket).
Value-add play with rent growth and operational efficiency upside cited.
stories.summary: A regional private equity group in joint venture with a local operator acquired Canyon Villas, a 122-unit seniors facility with 122 independent/assisted living beds and 133 licensed memory care beds in San Diego's Clairemont neighborhood. The transaction generated multiple competitive offers and is positioned for operational and rent-growth value creation.
stories.impact: Seniors housing demand in San Diego is robust and attracting institutional PE capital—a parallel asset class to multifamily. However, limited direct impact unless Trammell Crow is pursuing seniors-focused development; Clairemont's desirability signals broader neighborhood gentrification and renter demand spillover from inner-city San Diego markets.

stories.title: Lee & Associates of Illinois Closes Four Office Suburban Chicago Leases
stories.excerpt: Lee & Associates has closed four office leases in Chicago’s western and northwest suburbs. Grant Bollman, senior vice president at Lee & Associates of Illinois, represented tenants in the transactions, which included Thomas Architects signing a 1,411-square-foot new lease in Arlington Heights and Thorndale Construction signing a 2,903-square-foot lease expansion in Naperville. Additionallu, TekPro Staffing signed a 2,577-square-foot lease expansion in Oak Brook, and Terrell Materials signed a 2,804-square-foot lease renewal in Westmont. “At a time when construction costs are high, tenants do what they can to avoid a relocation and obtain solid economics to make their current space work for a longer period of time,” said Bollman. “The East-West Corridor in particular has been able to attract and retain tenants and achieve moderately healthy market conditions because of the diversity of tenants that reside there, including the smaller users we assisted with these transactions.” The post Lee & Associates of Illinois Closes Four Office Suburban Chicago Leases appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Four suburban Chicago office leases closed: Arlington Heights, Naperville, Oak Brook, Westmont.
Mix of new, expansion, and renewal; 1.4K–2.9K SF per transaction; East-West Corridor.
Tenants avoiding relocation due to high construction costs; seeking renewal at existing sites.
stories.summary: Lee & Associates of Illinois closed four office leases in Chicago's western and northwest suburbs totaling approximately 9.7K SF. Transactions included Thomas Architects (1.4K SF new lease, Arlington Heights), Thorndale Construction (2.9K SF expansion, Naperville), TekPro Staffing (2.6K SF expansion, Oak Brook), and Terrell Materials (2.8K SF renewal, Westmont). High construction costs are prompting tenants to renew rather than relocate.
stories.impact: Suburban Chicago office stickiness and modest new demand reflect cost avoidance behavior but mask underlying tenant weakness. For multifamily developers, this signals that white-collar employment in east-west corridor is stabilizing but not expanding—limiting near-term rent-growth catalysts in suburbs. Multifamily should remain focused on transit-oriented and urban-core Chicago locations with younger demographic draw.

stories.title: Ken Griffin Seals $3.3B Construction Loan for Manhattan Office Tower
stories.excerpt: Billionaire money manager Ken Griffin now has a firm financial investment in Midtown Manhattan months after a public feud with New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani. Griffin, as part of a joint venture with Vornado Realty Trust and Rudin, has landed $3.3 billion of construction financing to develop a 66-story office tower at 350 Park Avenue, the sponsorship announced Wednesday. A lending syndicate led by Wells Fargo and J.P. Morgan Chase originated the loan for the 1.9 million-square-foot building. Griffin will have a 60 percent stake in 350 Park Avenue under the newly formed JV with Vornado holding 36 percent and Rudin 4 percent, the companies also announced. Griffin’s Citadel financial firm will lease 1.05 million square feet in the new office tower, which is slated for completion in 2032. The remaining 850,000 square feet on the building’s upper floors will be marketed to other tenants, according to the New York Post, which first reported the loan. The 350 Park deal closed on the heels of Mamdani posting a social media video in April touting a tax on pieds-à-terre in front of Griffin’s penthouse at 220 Central Park South. The move sparked sharp criticism of Mamdani from leading figures in the commercial real estate industry, including Vornado CEO Steven Roth during his first-quarter earnings call in early May. Wells Fargo and J.P. Morgan did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Ken Griffin secures $3.3B construction loan for 350 Park Avenue (66-story, 1.9M SF).
Wells Fargo + JPMorgan syndication; completion 2032; Citadel leases 1.05M SF.
Griffin 60%, Vornado 36%, Rudin 4%; Manhattan office investment despite mayoral tensions.
stories.summary: A lending syndicate led by Wells Fargo and JPMorgan Chase provided $3.3 billion in construction financing for 350 Park Avenue, a 66-story, 1.9M SF office tower in Midtown Manhattan. Griffin's Citadel will occupy 1.05M SF (60% JV stake); Vornado holds 36% and Rudin 4%. Completion is slated for 2032.
stories.impact: Large-scale office construction financing signals lender willingness to underwrite long-cycle Manhattan development and confidence in anchor-tenant credit (Citadel). However, massive office delivery in 2032 will compete with existing midtown stock and remote-work headwinds; for multifamily, this implies sustained Manhattan office oversupply will compress office conversion economics and keep multifamily rents resilient as office-to-residential conversions remain limited. Urban Manhattan residential demand remains tied to white-collar job density—monitor Citadel's actual occupancy.

stories.title: Canadian Investor Buys Two Hotels in Palm Beach County for More Than $48M
stories.excerpt: Brasswater paid more than $48 million to buy two Hampton Inns hotels in Palm Beach County, Fla., from Hospitality Investors Trust, property records show. In the biggest transaction, the Montrael-based firm paid at least $29 million for the 164-room Hampton Inn & Suites Boynton Beach. The 102,476-square-foot property was built in 1997 on a 3-acre property at 1475 Gateway Boulevard, about a mile west of Interstate 95. Secondly, Brasswater bought the 110-room Hampton Inn West Palm Beach Florida Turnpike for more than $19 million. The 68,800-square-foot asset sits just west of Florida Turnpike, adjacent to Okeechobee Boulevard at 2025 Vista Parkway. It was built on a 2.4-acre site in 2001. The total of the recent purchases is likely higher to include the furniture and business operations of the Hilton properties, which is often not reflected in public deeds that only value the real estate. New York-based Axonic Capital supplied a debt package backing both hotels totaling $42.2 million. Fairfax, Va.-based Hospitality Investors Trust had purchased the two hotels for a combined $43.6 million in 2015. The recent sales come as Hospitality Investors Trust has been selling off some of its South Florida properties. Starting in June, it sold a 117-room Hampton Inn in Palm Beach Gardens for $14.3 million, followed by the $9.8 million sale of another 106-room Hampton Inn in Deerfield Beach. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Brasswater (Montreal) acquires two Hampton Inns in Palm Beach County; $48M+ total.
Boynton Beach 164 rooms ($29M+), West Palm Beach 110 rooms ($19M+); built 1997, 2001.
Axonic Capital $42.2M debt package; value-add play in hospitality market.
stories.summary: Brasswater, a Montreal-based investor, purchased two Hampton Inn properties in Palm Beach County for more than $48 million. The Boynton Beach property (164 rooms, 102.5K SF, built 1997) sold for at least $29 million; the West Palm Beach property (110 rooms, 68.8K SF, built 2001) for more than $19 million. Axonic Capital provided $42.2 million in debt financing.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily impact (hospitality asset class). However, foreign capital inflow into South Florida lodging signals confidence in the region's tourism and business-travel recovery, which typically correlates with workforce housing demand and corporate relocations—watch for follow-on multifamily M&A activity in Palm Beach County if tourism and employment accelerate.

stories.title: Mexican Eatery Casa Carmen to Open Third Manhattan Location
stories.excerpt: Mexican restaurant Casa Carmen is opening its third Manhattan location in Midtown East, Commercial Observer has learned. The restaurant concept started by chef Carmen “Titita” Ramírez Degollado signed a 15-year, 6,917-square-foot lease to serve up traditional Mexican cuisine at Sage’s 437 Madison Avenue, according to tenant broker Retail by MONA as well as the landlord. Asking rent for the space was $200 per square foot, according to Retail by MONA. “Casa Carmen is a natural fit for 437 Madison Avenue and our hospitality-driven approach to the workplace,” Michael Lenchner, director of leasing at Sage, said in a statement. “We are continually looking for ways to make the workplace experience more convenient, engaging and enjoyable for our tenants and their employees. Bringing a restaurant of Casa Carmen’s caliber into the building gives our members and tenants another exceptional option right outside their office doors.” CBRE’s Matthew Chmielecki and Preston Cannon negotiated on behalf of the landlord, while John DiGangi of Retail by MONA represented Casa Carmen in the deal. CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “Midtown is seeing a new wave of investment and energy, driven by major corporate headquarters, office activity and the continued evolution of the neighborhood,” Brandon Singer, founder and CEO of Retail by MONA, said in a statement. “As more companies make significant commitments to the area, we’re seeing opportunities for restaurant and hospitality concepts that can serve the growing demand from office workers, residents and visitors alike.” The New York Post briefly mentioned the deal in an Oct. 11 writeup but provided no details. Casa Carmen has existing locations at 114 Franklin Street in Tribeca and 5 West 21st Street in the Flatiron District. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Casa Carmen (Mexican eatery) signs 15-year lease at 437 Madison Avenue, Midtown East.
6,917 SF at $200/SF asking rent; Sage landlord; restaurant expansion into third NYC location.
Ground-floor retail activation in office building; hospitality/food tenant diversification.
stories.summary: Casa Carmen, a Mexican restaurant concept founded by chef Carmen 'Titita' Ramírez Degollado, signed a 15-year, 6,917 SF lease at 437 Madison Avenue in Midtown East at $200/SF annual rent. This is the restaurant's third Manhattan location; Sage landlord positioned it as workplace amenity to attract office tenants.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance; office/retail activation story. However, Midtown East's ability to attract third-party dining concepts signals office-building amenitization and potential recovery in food-service employment—indirect support for Manhattan residential demand if office occupancy rebounds alongside tenant satisfaction initiatives.

stories.title: L.A. Multifamily Sales Jump 44%
stories.excerpt: Los Angeles County multifamily investment sales are up after the third quarter while average rent and occupancy rates appear to be stuck in neutral. Sales volume for multifamily properties with 50 or more units reached $3.3 billion so far on the year, up 44 percent from the same period in 2025, while the average sale price declined to $357,085 per unit, according to a new Colliers market report. At the same time, L.A.’s apartment occupancy rate held at 94.1 percent in the third quarter, unchanged from the previous quarter, and down only slightly from 94.4 percent a year earlier. Average monthly effective rent increased by $6 to $2,428 per unit in the third quarter, but it is back to the same rate after the third quarter of 2025. Colliers pinned both the annual decline in occupancy and the static rent in part to new construction. Colliers estimates developers added 4,277 units during the third quarter, which is about 72 percent more than in the second quarter. Absorption of these units totaled 3,809 units, up significantly from 2,429 the previous quarter and 2,360 a year ago. However, the apartment construction pipeline is shrinking. There were 23,426 units under construction at the end of the third quarter, down from 24,877 in the second quarter and 25,421 a year earlier. L.A. County has completed more than 58,800 apartments since the second quarter of 2021, per Colliers. The Westside remained the most expensive area, with average effective rents at $3,336 per month, despite occupancy of 92.9 percent. The submarket also had the largest development pipeline with 5,894 units under construction. The Hollywood and Mid-Wilshire neighborhoods recorded an average rent of $2,355 and occupancy of 92 percent, the second-lowest occupancy rate for the top submarkets. It also led the region in new deliveries with 1,869 units added during the quarter, while 5,113 units are under construction. Downtown and the areas going into Central L.A. posted the market’s lowest occupancy rate
bullets: LA County multifamily sales up 44% YTD to $3.3B; average price $357K/unit (down from prior).
Q3 occupancy 94.1% (flat QoQ, down 0.3% YoY); effective rent $2,428 (+$6 MoM, flat YoY).
4,277 units delivered Q3 (72% higher than Q2); absorption 3,809 units; new supply dampening rent.
stories.summary: Los Angeles County multifamily investment sales reached $3.3 billion YTD, up 44 percent from 2025, though average per-unit prices declined to $357K. Occupancy held steady at 94.1% in Q3 (flat QoQ, -30 bps YoY), and effective rent increased only $6 to $2,428/month (flat vs. Q3 2025). Developers delivered 4,277 units in Q3 (72% higher than Q2), with absorption of 3,809 units; Colliers attributes rent stagnation to new supply influx.
stories.impact: LA multifamily market is oversupplied on the back of elevated development activity; rent growth is stalled despite healthy occupancy due to unit churn. For Trammell Crow, this signals a critical window to slow acquisitions/starts in LA or pivot toward higher-barrier coastal markets (Santa Monica, Culver City, Downtown LA) with limited new supply. Suburban LA (Westchester, etc.) faces competitive pressure; near-term pricing power is weak, and new projects will face 12–18 month lease-up headwinds. Capital deployment should prioritize markets with stricter zoning (SF Bay, NYC, DC) where new supply is constrained.
